statements.t: As of October 30, 2026, we are party to forward purchase agreements for 34 aircraft with deliveries expected between November 2026 and 2028.

The engines from these aircraft will be retained for future overhaul cost mitigation and may be sold on an opportunistic basis if we determine the engine has no better economic use in our operating fleet.
Integration of Sun Country’s business with our existing business is underway and is expected to be a complex, costly, and time-consuming process.
We believe the combination will enhance our network breadth, operational flexibility, and ability to respond to demand shifts, while supporting the passenger and charter operations of both airlines.
We have applied with the FAA for a single operating certificate ("SOC") which we currently expect will be obtained in 2028.
Our ability to combine operations will be limited until we receive a single operating certificate and there are joint collective bargaining agreements in place with the various unionized work groups.

Once the SOC is granted by the FAA and the combined PSS is implemented (which is currently expected in 2028), we believe we will be able to begin to capture more of the revenue and cost synergies sought from the transaction.
We have not used financial derivative products to hedge against fuel price volatility, nor do we have any plans to do so in the future.
We expect to continue to manage our peak period utilization as the demand environment allows.
We have also announced Allegiant First, a new premium seating tier scheduled to debut on future MAX deliveries, with service expected to begin in spring 2027.

We believe this new aircraft purchase is complementary with our low-cost strategy based on our intent to retain ownership of the aircraft, the longer useful life for depreciation purposes, and expected fuel savings and operational reliability from the use of these new aircraft.
We currently expect four aircraft to be delivered to us in the last three months of 2026 with the remaining aircraft under contract to be delivered in 2027 and 2028.

Among other new and modified terms, that new agreement provides for increased compensation and enhanced benefits to the Allegiant Air pilot group and contains improvements to the scheduling process which we expect will increase pilot productivity.

We believe we have more than adequate liquidity resources through our cash, cash equivalent and short-term investment balances, existing aircraft financing facilities, our undrawn capacity under existing credit facilities, operating cash flows and anticipated access to liquidity, to meet our current contractual obligations and remain in compliance with the debt covenants in our existing financing agreements for…
We will continue to consider raising funds through debt financing as needed to fund capital expenditures.
We expect to continue to experience material increases in fuel costs while these circumstances persist.

estimates.t: Except as set forth below, there were no material changes to our critical accounting estimates during the nine months ended September 30, 2026.

estimates.name: Business Combination Accounting
estimates.t: To record the value of assets acquired and liabilities assumed as a result of our acquisition of Sun Country on May 13, 2026, we have performed a purchase price allocation utilizing the best information available to management.

statements.t: "Looking ahead to the fourth quarter, 72 percent of our ASMs are scheduled on high-demand peak days, and fuel-efficient MAX aircraft are expected to account for 20 percent of our combined capacity.
With strong booking momentum, we remain confident in our 2026 full-year adjusted earnings per share guidance of greater than $6.00, despite elevated fuel costs.
Together, we are building the nation’s leading leisure carrier, and we look forward to sharing our integration milestones and long-term financial framework at our Investor Day on December 7."

The Company is not able to reconcile these Non-GAAP financial figures without unreasonable effort because the special charge adjustments will not be known until the end of the indicated future periods and any range of projected values would be too broad to be meaningful.

The numbers include aircraft expected to be in service at the end of each period and exclude both aircraft that we expect to take delivery of but not to be placed in service until a subsequent period and aircraft in temporary storage.
A live broadcast of the conference call will be available via the Company’s Investor Relations website homepage at http://ir.allegiantair.com .
